transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you. Well, what finally pushed me to make this appointment is work, mostly. I manage a medical clinic, and I can start an EPIC quality report, or sit down in a clinic metrics meeting with every intention of tracking it. I really do go in meaning to focus. 

But honestly, the new EPIC update they rolled out last month has been such a headache. The billing codes don't sync right with the front desk software anymore, and my receptionist, Brenda—she's been with us for twelve years, lovely woman, makes the best zucchini bread, but she absolutely refuses to learn the new keyboard shortcuts. So I spend half my morning fixing her batches, and it just throws my whole day off. 

But anyway, what I was saying is, I'll be in these meetings or looking at the report, and within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far away. I'll suddenly realize I’m rereading the exact same column of numbers for the fifth time, or I’ve completely missed the whole point of the discussion.
Do you also find it hard to focus or stay attentive in situations outside of work, like at home or during conversations with friends?

Outside of work? Um, I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed it being an issue at home or with friends, to be honest. 

Like, I was just having coffee with my friend Martha on Sunday. She just got one of those Goldendoodle puppies, and honestly, I don't know how she manages that kind of energy level at our age. She was telling me all about the breeder she used, who apparently lives all the way up in Vermont. I actually went to Vermont once, years ago, right after I finished my bachelor's. We did one of those autumn foliage tours, and the colors were just incredible. We stayed at this little bed and breakfast that made their own maple syrup, and they served it over these huge, thick pecan waffles every morning... 

But, um, wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, focusing during conversations. Yeah, I don't really know if I zone out with Martha or when I'm at the house. I just haven't really thought about it or noticed it happening.
When you're at home, do you ever notice yourself losing focus while doing things like reading a book, watching a show, or following instructions for something like a recipe or home project?

Um, reading or watching a show? No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed that happening. Like, I watch TV in the evenings... we actually just started that new historical drama on PBS. The one set in the 1890s? The costumes are just absolutely stunning. I was telling my sister just the other day, I have no idea how they manage all that intricate beadwork by hand. 

My grandmother used to do beadwork, actually. She made this incredible little clutch purse for my wedding, with these tiny pearl beads. It took her six months to finish it. We had a spring wedding, right when the tulips were blooming, so the pearls looked just lovely with the flowers. We had the reception at this old botanical garden... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, I don't really have trouble following a show or a recipe or anything like that. At least, not that I can think of.
Do you ever feel restless or have trouble relaxing, even when you're not at work?

Restless? Um, no, I wouldn't say so. I don't really feel antsy or anything like that when I'm trying to relax at home. 

I mean, I do like to keep busy on the weekends, but that's just because I enjoy it. Like this past Saturday, I decided to finally organize the hall closet. It's been a disaster since we put the winter coats away. We have these heavy wool peacoats—my husband insists on buying them from this specific catalogue that still ships out of Maine. He’s been ordering from them since the 90s, back when you actually had to mail in a paper form with a check. I remember the first time he ordered one, it was right before we took that trip to Chicago. 

Oh, Chicago in November is just brutally cold. The wind coming off the lake goes right through you. We tried to walk to the Navy Pier and we only made it about three blocks before we had to duck into a diner for coffee. They had the most amazing cherry pie there, though. I've actually been trying to find a recipe that replicates that crust, it was so flaky...

Um, but what were you asking? Oh, relaxing. Yeah, no, I don't have trouble relaxing. I feel fine when I'm just sitting around.
When you're at home relaxing, like when you're reading a book or watching a show, have you ever noticed yourself getting distracted or having trouble staying focused on what you're doing?

Um, reading or watching a show? No, I don't think I get distracted. I mean, I love a good book. I just finished this mystery novel set in the English countryside, right in the Cotswolds. Have you ever been? Oh, it's just picturesque. The author described these little stone cottages with the thatched roofs so perfectly, I felt like I was right back there. 

My husband and I went for our twentieth anniversary. We rented a car, which was terrifying because he had to drive on the left side of the road. He kept drifting too close to the hedges. But we found this little pub that served the best fish and chips I've ever had. Wrapped in newspaper and everything. They used a local ale for the batter...

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Distracted while reading? No, I don't think so. I can usually just sit and read or watch TV without a problem.
Do you ever find yourself losing focus or having trouble paying attention during conversations with other people, even outside of work?

Um, outside of work? Well, it definitely happens at work, I can tell you that. I'm a health services manager, and I'll be in a meeting... like, a medical director or one of my care coordinators will be talking right to me. And I'm looking right at them, nodding along, making eye contact, the whole nine yards. But then, when they finish, I have to ask them to repeat the action item because the words just... they didn't stay with me. It's like they just floated right past my ears. 

It actually happened with Dr. Evans just last week. He was going over the new scheduling protocols for the outpatient clinic. He’s always so particular about scheduling. He insists on having this specific 15-minute buffer between initial consults and follow-ups, which, honestly, is a nightmare for the front desk staff to manage. I remember one of our receptionists, Sarah—sweet girl, just had a baby boy, actually. She named him Oliver. Such a cute name, right? She brought him into the office last month and he had these little chubby cheeks... 

Anyway, Sarah was in tears trying to figure out how to make Dr. Evans' schedule work with the new electronic health record system we just rolled out. The rollout has been an absolute disaster, by the way. The IT guys were here until 9 PM on a Friday trying to fix the server... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, conversations outside of work. You know, I guess I mostly notice it at the office, with the directors and coordinators. I'm not really sure if it happens as much with my friends or family.
When you're talking with friends or family members, do you ever find yourself having trouble keeping track of what they're saying or realizing later that you missed parts of the conversation?

Um, friends and family... I don't really know if I do that with them. I guess I haven't really noticed it. 

I mean, I talk to my sister on the phone every Sunday. She lives down in Florida now, near Sarasota. She moved there about five years ago because she couldn't take the winters up here anymore. She's got this beautiful little lanai attached to her house, all screened in so the bugs don't get you. The mosquitoes down there are just enormous. When we went to visit her last February, I got bitten on the ankle and it swelled up like a golf ball. I had to go to this little urgent care clinic right off the highway. The doctor there was actually very nice, he went to medical school in the Caribbean, St. George's, I think? We got to talking about it because my niece was thinking about applying there for vet school... 

But, um, keeping track of what they're saying? I don't think I really miss things when I'm talking to my sister or my husband. At least, they haven't complained about it to me!
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um, feeling down? No, I don't think so. I mean, I still enjoy things just fine. Like my gardening! I've been spending so much time out in the yard lately. We finally got the soil right for the hydrangeas. They need a very specific pH to get that really vibrant blue color, you know. I had to go to the garden center three times to get the right soil acidifier. The guy who works there, Kevin, he's so helpful. He actually used to work in landscaping before he hurt his back. He was telling me all about this new physical therapy regimen he's on, which sounded a lot like what my husband had to do when he threw his back out shoveling snow a few winters ago. We had that massive blizzard, remember? The one that dumped like two feet overnight? 

Anyway, what were you asking? Oh, depressed or losing interest. No, I don't feel depressed. I still love doing my usual things.

Do you ever notice yourself losing focus or having trouble staying on task when you're doing something that isn't work-related, like following a conversation at a family gathering or finishing a task around the house?

Um, at a family gathering or around the house? Well, I don't know about around the house so much, but I guess I do struggle with staying on task at work. Honestly, that's what finally pushed me to make this appointment. 

I'll sit down to do an EPIC quality report, or I'll be in one of those long clinic metrics meetings. And I go in with every intention of tracking exactly what's going on. I'll have my notepad out, my favorite pen—it's this gel pen I found at a stationery shop in Boston when we went for my niece's graduation. She went to BU, studied communications. Boston is such a great walking city, though the traffic is just horrific. We got stuck in the Ted Williams Tunnel for over an hour on the way to the airport...

But anyway, I'll be in the meeting, or looking at the report, and within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far away. I'll catch myself just staring at the screen, rereading the same row of numbers over and over, or I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the entire point of whatever the medical director was just discussing. It's incredibly frustrating.
